note: Interface types: the bundles of signals a package's interfaces are instances of (each package's ports.json, under "interfaces"). Signals are named from the device's own side, so two devices connect by the type's joins: one's SDO to the other's SDI. Where a signal has a direction, it is the controller's; a target's is the reverse. Whether a connection needs more than wires (pull-ups, a level shifter) is for interface rules, not these types.

i2c.note: A bus: any number of targets on one controller's two lines, each at its own address.

spi.note: A bus: targets share SCK, SDO and SDI, and each has its own CS. A device that only listens or only talks needs one data line.

uart.note: Point to point. Flow control (RTS, CTS) is optional, as is either direction.

pwm.note: One PWM slice: two channels at one frequency. Either channel alone will do.

logic.note: One digital line. An instance says which way it goes (dir: in, out, bidir) and how it drives (push_pull, open_drain, tristate).

pio.note: A programmable I/O block: on any pins it reaches, software state machines can act as any digital interface (it lists them under implements). Use one only when no hardware block fits: it costs state machines and firmware.
